authority: advisory; Android source, target code, installed SDK, and executed evidence remain authoritative

entries.applies_when: Any bundled knowledge is used for SDD planning, implementation or validation; this defines artifact ownership and evidence interpretation.
The active slice uses res/layout XML, ViewBinding/DataBinding, RecyclerView/ViewHolder, visibility rules, Android drawable XML, or View-based form controls.
The active slice uses CoordinatorLayout, AppBarLayout, CollapsingToolbarLayout, nested scrolling, pager-tab coordination, anchored controls, or persistent sheets.
The Android behavior contains RxJava types, Subjects, schedulers, disposables, Flowable backpressure, or operators migrated to coroutines/Flow.
The active behavior uses Flow, StateFlow, SharedFlow, Channel, callbackFlow, one-shot effects, replay, or multiple collectors.
The active behavior starts, owns, cancels, retries, or outlives coroutine work, lifecycle scopes, ViewModel scopes, callbacks, or background work.
The source retries, backs off, throttles, debounces, buffers, conflates, drops, switches to latest, or processes burst input.
Focused tests cover suspend work, delayed work, hot streams, lifecycle-owned tasks, injected dispatchers, or virtual time.
The slice crosses commonMain and platform source sets, introduces expect/actual, or binds a system/native capability.
The target declares ohosArm64, ohosX64, ohosMain, harmonyApp, or publish*BinariesToHarmonyApp tasks.
The Android behavior reaches a system service, permission, OS side effect, native library, Android/JVM-only SDK, ArkTS Kit, or C API.
The slice affects permissions, EntryAbility/window setup, system bars, insets, IME, orientation, full-screen transitions, or device networking.

Harmony is required, the target exposes MPCore ArkUIViewController/Compose back APIs, and the active slice preserves or introduces a user-visible route stack, has observable Android back behavior, or the approved Spec explicitly requires platform back or an edge-back gesture.
The active slice uses HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket, Ktor, Retrofit/OkHttp migration, auth refresh, upload/download, or generated API clients on native targets.
The target publishes KMP binaries/resources to harmonyApp, packages HAP, writes files/databases, links native libraries, or declares Harmony ABIs.
The slice uses screenshot/UI runtime evidence, animations, clocks, remote images, asynchronous rendering, or deterministic fixtures.
